checkpoint.title: If true, at the end of the propagation the state is saved in Output/checkpoint (header.json + one binary file per MPI rank) for a restart. Only for RK

restart_directory.title: If not empty, directory of a checkpoint (e.g. ../run/Output/checkpoint): the propagation starts from the saved state and time, with the same number of MPI ranks and the same input (dt, grid, lasers, phonons). Run it in a new directory: the txt outputs start at the restart time

decay.title: decay rate of the density matrix

decay_units.title: Units used for the decay rate of the density matrix

fermienergy_units.title: Units used for the Fermi energy of the system

coulomb.title: If true, we go beyond IPA using either RPA or HSEX.

method.title: If ipa, non-interactiong particles are considered. If RPA, we consider only the Hartree term for the interaction. If hsex, both Hartree and screened Fock are taken into account.

opengap.title: Gap value, if we want to open more gap

opengap_units.title: Units used for the gap we want to open

read_interaction.title: If true, electron-electron interactions are read from barecoulomb.txt and screencoulomb.txt.

bare_file.title: Path of the bare Coulomb interaction

hartree.title: If false, the Hartree term is skipped in the mean field (with method hsex: screened exchange only)

screen_file.title: Path of the screened Coulomb interaction

r0.title: r0 screening length for RK potential

r0_units.title: Units for the Time resolution used for propagating Density Matrix

hartree_centers.title: Positions of the Wannier functions used for the Hartree term: wannier = their centers; atoms = the centers closer than hartree_center_tolerance are grouped and moved to the mean of the group (the atom), so that all the orbitals of an atom have the same on-site interaction and the Hartree matrix is positive semidefinite

hartree_cutoff_factor.title: The bare interaction of the Hartree term is saturated below hartree_cutoff_factor times the minimum distance between two Wannier centers on different sites, so that the on-site interaction is V(factor * d_min). With 1 the on-site interaction equals the one between the closest centers and the Hartree matrix can have negative eigenvalues (rho0 unstable); 0.5 with hartree_centers = atoms makes it positive semidefinite for MoS2

hartree_center_tolerance.title: Distance (angstrom) below which two Wannier centers belong to the same atom, for hartree_centers = atoms

grid.title: Dimension of the k grid (R as well) used for the simulation

qgrid.title: Dimension of the q grid used for the simulation

filledbands.title: Number of filled bands for the simulation (ideally will be either this of fermienergy

dt.title: Time resolution used for propagating Density Matrix

gradient_space.title: Space where the gradient with respect to k is evaluated

dt_units.title: Units for the Time resolution used for propagating Density Matrix

printresolution.title: Time steps needed to print in hdf5 and observables

write_velocity_sigma.title: If true, Output/Velocity_sigma.txt: the mean-field part of the velocity, (i[Sigma, r] + grad_k Sigma)/V, already included in Velocity.txt

printresolution_h5.title: If > 0, the hdf5 matrices are printed every printresolution_h5 time steps, whether the lasers are on or off

printresolution_pulse.title: Time steps needed to print in hdf5 and observables during the pulse

initialtime_units.title: Units for the Time resolution used for Initial time of the simulation

finaltime_units.title: Units for the Time resolution used for Final time of the simulation

solver.title: Solver used for time propagation of the Density Matrix

order.title: Order of the Solver used for time propagation of the Density Matrix: 4 for RK, 3 or 4 for AB, 4 for Magnus

peierls.title: If true, we propagate the EOM in the Peierls gauge

toprint.title: Big quantities that we want to print

DMk_wannier.title: true if you want to print DM in k, wannier gauge

DMk_bloch.title: true if you want to print DM in k, bloch gauge

fullH.title: true if you want to print H=H0+Er in k, wannier gauge

SelfEnergy.title: true if you want to print the self energy in k, wannier gauge

DM_R.title: true if you want to print the equilibrium DM in R (Output/DM<rank>.txt, txt)

phonons.title: Lattice coupled to the electrons at the mean-field (Ehrenfest) level, from the Wannier representation of EPW (see src/Phonons/EHRENFEST.md)

enabled.title: If true, the lattice at q = Gamma is propagated together with the electrons

epw_directory.title: Directory of the EPW calculation (epwwrite = .true.) of the bare coupling g_b, with epwdata.fmt, wigner.fmt, crystal.fmt and prefix.epmatwp. The Wannier functions must be the ones of tb_file. g_b gives the force on the atoms, and it is the coupling felt by the electrons if epw_directory_screened is empty

epmatwp.title: Name of the file prefix.epmatwp in epw_directory; if empty, the only *.epmatwp file of the directory

epw_directory_screened.title: Directory of the EPW calculation of the screened coupling g_s (optional, same Wannier functions). If given, the electrons feel u.g_s and the mean field of rho - rho_BO (the static screening is already in g_s); if empty, they feel u.g_b and the mean field of rho - rho0

epmatwp_screened.title: Name of the file prefix.epmatwp in epw_directory_screened; if empty, the only *.epmatwp file of the directory

dyn_file.title: Dynamical matrix of ph.x at Gamma (text format, e.g. prefix.dyn1): masses and force constants. Only with one q point; alternative to ifc_file

ifc_file.title: Interatomic force constants of q2r.x (text format, e.g. prefix.fc), alternative to dyn_file: masses and force constants K(q) on the q grid of the simulation (each q must be on the q grid of q2r). Needed if the q grid (qgrid) has more than one point; the lattice has one wavevector per point of the q grid

initial_displacement_q.title: Wavevector q0 of the initial displacement, crystal coordinates (it must be a point of the q grid, together with -q0): the atom in the cell R is displaced by initial_displacement*cos(q0.R), R lattice vector. [0, 0, 0] = the same displacement in every cell

spin_degeneracy.title: Spin degeneracy of the bands (2 for a model without spin, 1 with spin-orbit): the force on the atoms is summed over the spin channels

damping_time.title: Decay time of the amplitude of the lattice oscillations (phenomenological); 0 = no damping

coupling_scale.title: Factor multiplying the electron-phonon coupling of EPW (0 = lattice decoupled from the electrons)

acoustic_sum_rule.title: Impose the acoustic sum rule on the force constants and remove the rigid translation from the electron-phonon coupling

adiabatic_reference.title: Adiabatic (Born-Oppenheimer) density matrix rho_BO(u): the force constants of ph.x already contain the static screening of the atoms by the electrons, so only rho - rho_BO pushes the atoms. static (recommended) = rho0 + static linear response of the electrons of the model to u, computed at the beginning (keeps the non-adiabatic correction Pi(omega) - Pi(0)); dynamic = density matrix propagated with the same displacements and no laser (removes also the non-adiabatic correction of the ground state)

adiabatic_coupling.title: Only with epw_directory_screened: how rho_BO is built. Dynamic reference, Hamiltonian of the propagated rho_BO: screened = H0 + u.g_s (static screening already in g_s, no mean field); bare = H0 + u.g_b + Sigma[rho_BO - rho0], the Born-Oppenheimer electrons of the model with their own mean field. Static reference: screened = rho0 + u.chi0 g_s; bare = rho0 + u.chi(0) g_b, static response of the bare model with its mean field. The electrons always feel u.g_s + Sigma[rho - rho_BO] and the atoms the force of g_b

initial_displacement.title: Initial displacement of the atoms, 3 cartesian components per atom (lattice at rest); empty = equilibrium

initial_displacement_cells.title: Initial displacement localized on some cells, alternative to initial_displacement (lattice at rest): list of objects {"R": [n1, n2, n3], "displacement": [3 cartesian components per atom]}, with R the lattice vector of the cell in crystal coordinates (integers) and displacement in initial_displacement_units. The atoms of the cell R are displaced by displacement, the other cells are at equilibrium. The pattern is periodic on the supercell of the q grid: u_mu(q) = 1/N_q sum_R displacement_mu(R) e^{-iq.R}. E.g. a seed that breaks the symmetry of the crystal for a self-trapped exciton

local_potential.title: External local potential at finite momentum, V(r,t) = amplitude*f(t)*cos(q.r) with f(t) = exp(-(t-t0)^2/(2 sigma^2)). In the Wannier basis it is diagonal: V_n(R) = amplitude*f(t)*cos(q.(R + tau_n)), with tau_n the Wannier centers. It needs a q grid that contains +q and -q

enabled.title: If true, the local potential is added to the Hamiltonian

q.title: Wave vector q of the potential, crystal coordinates of the reciprocal lattice. Must be a point of the q grid, different from 0

t0.title: Center of the Gaussian envelope f(t)

sigma.title: Width of the Gaussian envelope f(t)

kpath.title: vertex of a path in k space where we want to print the band structure

intensity_units.title: Units for intensity of the laser

frequency_units.title: Units for frequency of the laser

wavelength_units.title: Units for wavelength of the laser

polarization.title: Polarization of the laser in cartesian coordinates

t0_units.title: Units for initial time of the laser

cycles.title: Number of cycles the sin2 laser last.
